claim: The Drosophila retina is composed of approximately 750 facets called ommatidia.
source: Drosophila retina is composed of approximately 750 facets called ommatidia (Cagan and Ready, 1989; Tepass and Harris, 2007), each of which includes four cone cells (C) embedded in two primary pigment cells (P), along with other cell types shared by neighboring ommatidia (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to previous work (Cagan and Ready, 1989; Tepass and Harris, 2007).

claim: Each ommatidium includes four cone cells embedded in two primary pigment cells.
source: Drosophila retina is composed of approximately 750 facets called ommatidia (Cagan and Ready, 1989; Tepass and Harris, 2007), each of which includes four cone cells (C) embedded in two primary pigment cells (P), along with other cell types shared by neighboring ommatidia (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text with citations and supported by Figure 1A,B showing the structure.

claim: The pattern of cone cells arrangement is strikingly similar to that of soap bubbles.
source: The pattern of cone cells arrangement is strikingly similar to that of soap bubbles (Hayashi and Carthew, 2004).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Hayashi and Carthew, 2004.

claim: Two classical Type I cadherins, E-cadherin and N-cadherin, are expressed in the retina.
source: Two classical Type I cadherins, E-cadherin (Ecad) and N-cadherin (Ncad) are expressed in the retina and specific expression of N-cadherin solely in cone cells governs the cone cell shape and arrangements (Hayashi and Carthew, 2004).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text with a citation to Hayashi and Carthew, 2004.

claim: Specific expression of N-cadherin solely in cone cells governs the cone cell shape and arrangements.
source: Two classical Type I cadherins, E-cadherin (Ecad) and N-cadherin (Ncad) are expressed in the retina and specific expression of N-cadherin solely in cone cells governs the cone cell shape and arrangements (Hayashi and Carthew, 2004).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Hayashi and Carthew, 2004.

claim: Ncad is localized at cone cell-cone cell contacts where it forms homophilic complexes.
source: As previously reported (Hayashi and Carthew, 2004), Ncad is localized at cone cell-cone cell contacts (C|C), where it forms homophilic complexes (Figure 1C, white arrowhead).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text with a citation and supported by Figure 1C showing the localization.

claim: Ncad is found at low level at the junctions between cone cell and primary pigment cell.
source: Ncad is also found at low level at the junctions between cone cell and primary pigment cell (C|P) (Figure 1C, cyan arrowhead and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing the localization.

claim: At C|P contacts, Ncad cannot form trans-homophilic bonds but cis-homophilic bonds, as it is expressed in cone cells but not in primary pigment cells.
source: At C|P contacts, Ncad cannot form trans-homophilic bonds but cis-homophilic bonds, as it is expressed in cone cells but not in primary pigment cells.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the differential expression pattern of Ncad.

claim: Ncad-Ecad trans-heterotypic bonds appear to be absent, as Ecad mutant cone cell loses contact from the neighbouring Ecad expressing primary pigment cell.
source: In addition, Ncad-Ecad trans-heterotypic bonds appear to be absent, as Ecad mutant cone cell loses contact from the neighbouring Ecad expressing primary pigment cell (Hayashi and Carthew, 2004).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Hayashi and Carthew, 2004.

claim: Ecad is present in all cell contacts albeit at different levels.
source: Ecad is present in all cell contacts albeit at different levels.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: Ecad concentration is lower at C|C relative to C|P and at primary pigment cell and primary pigment cell contacts (P|P).
source: Ecad concentration is lower at C|C relative to C|P and at primary pigment cell and primary pigment cell contacts (P|P) (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1D showing the distribution.

claim: MyoII is enriched at cell contacts and is also present as apical mesh at a lower concentration.
source: As reported earlier (Warner and Longmore, 2009; Yashiro et al., 2014; Deng et al., 2015), Phospho-Myosin-II light chain antibodies show a punctate distribution, but overall the three markers indicate that MyoII is enriched at cell contacts and is also present as apical mesh at a lower concentration.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Warner and Longmore, 2009; Yashiro et al., 2014; Deng et al., 2015.

claim: Ncad mutation in one or multiple cone cells results in significant cell shape changes.
source: Ncad mutation in one or multiple cone cells results in significant cell shape changes (Figure 1F), as reported earlier (Hayashi and Carthew, 2004).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text with a citation and supported by Figure 1F showing the shape changes.

claim: Shape variations are dependent on the numbers and combinations of wildtype and NcadM19 cone cells in the mosaic ommatidia.
source: Shape variations are dependent on the numbers and combinations of wildtype and NcadM19 cone cells in the mosaic ommatidia (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1F showing different mosaic configurations.

claim: In a full NcadM19 ommatidium, the four cone cells acquire a cruciform shape rather than the normal diamond shape.
source: In a full NcadM19 ommatidium, the four cone cells acquire a cruciform shape rather than the normal diamond shape (last and first image respectively in Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1F showing the shape difference.

claim: Reduction in cell contact length and change in angles suggests that adhesion by homophilic bonding of Ncad causes a significant expansion of contacts between cone cells.
source: Reduction in cell contact length (Figure 1F, yellow arrowhead) and change in angles (compare first and the last image of Figure 1F, magenta arrowhead) suggests that adhesion by homophilic bonding of Ncad causes a significant expansion of contacts between cone cells.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1F showing the measurements.

claim: At wildtype and NcadM19 cone cell contact, there is a significant increase in MyoII level.
source: For instance, at wildtype and NcadM19 cone cell contact, there is a significant increase in MyoII level (Figure 1G, yellow arrowhead).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1G showing the MyoII levels.

claim: The loss of Ncad induces change in MyoII concentrations, suggesting a possible contribution of MyoII contractility in shaping cone cell patterns.
source: So, the loss of Ncad induces change in MyoII concentrations, suggesting a possible contribution of MyoII contractility in shaping cone cell patterns (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1G showing the MyoII distribution.

claim: MyoII at contacts between primary pigment cells, P(E)|P(E), was found 1.8-fold higher than at C(E,N)|C(E,N) contacts.
source: MyoII at contacts between primary pigment cells, P(E)|P(E), was found 1.8-fold higher than at C(E,N)|C(E,N) contacts (Figure 2A–C, Supplementary file 1 - table 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A–C and Supplementary file 1 - table 1 showing the quantification.

claim: Differences in MyoII concentrations at contact are dependent on Ncad expression in the cells.
source: Our data indicates that differences in MyoII concentrations at contact are dependent on Ncad expression in the cells.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the experimental observations.

claim: MyoII levels are uncorrelated with Ecad levels.
source: However, MyoII levels are uncorrelated with Ecad levels, ruling out this possibility (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G and H).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1G and H showing the lack of correlation.

claim: MyoII level anti-correlates with cell contact length.
source: MyoII level anti-correlates with cell contact length (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G,H), which is consistent with the idea that MyoII regulates length.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1G,H showing the anti-correlation.

claim: F-actin is mostly apical and junctional like MyoII, but its distribution does not strictly correlate with that of MyoII.
source: Thus, we stained for F-actin using phalloidin and found that F-actin is mostly apical and junctional like MyoII, but its distribution does not strictly correlate with that of MyoII; homotypic C(E,N)|C(E,N) contacts show higher F-actin level than C(E,N)|P(E), C(E,N)|C(E), P(E)|P(E) and C(E)|C(E) contacts (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C showing the F-actin distribution.

claim: Tension at C(E,N)|C(E) contacts was the highest while tension at C(E,N)|C(E,N) contacts was the lowest.
source: We found that tension at C(E,N)|C(E) contacts was the highest while tension at C(E,N)|C(E,N) contacts was the lowest (Figure 2J,K).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2J,K showing the tension measurements.

claim: Tension values correlate with the levels of MyoII.
source: These values correlate with the levels of MyoII (compare Figure 2C and J or Figure 2F and K) and are consistent with the hypothesis that MyoII is a major determinant of interfacial tension.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by comparing Figure 2C and J or Figure 2F and K.

claim: Homophilic Ncad at homotypic contact reduces MyoII levels.
source: We observed high level of Ncad at homotypic contacts (C(E,N)|C(E,N)) which also exhibit the lowest concentration of MyoII, by 1.8 fold lower than the P(E)|P(E) cell contacts. This suggests that homophilic Ncad at homotypic contact reduces MyoII levels (Figure 2A,C), in agreement with the idea that cadherin lowers interfacial tension at cell contacts (Maître and Heisenberg, 2013).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A,C showing the MyoII levels and a citation to Maître and Heisenberg, 2013.

claim: Unbound Ncad at heterotypic contact signals to MyoII and induces its accumulation.
source: At heterotypic contacts (C(E,N)|P(E)), where Ncad cannot form transhomophilic bond, Ncad was found at very low level (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and MyoII at a higher level than at any other contact (Figure 2A,C). This suggests that unbound Ncad at heterotypic contact signals to MyoII and induces its accumulation.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, and Figure 2A,C showing the Ncad and MyoII levels.

claim: Ncad misexpression in one of the primary pigment cell affected the shape of cone cells in contact with it.
source: Ncad misexpression in one of the primary pigment cell affected the shape of cone cells in contact with it (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3A,B showing the shape changes.

claim: Homophilic Ncad was detected at the C(E,N)|P(E,N+) contacts.
source: Homophilic Ncad was detected at the C(E,N)|P(E,N+) contacts (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and A', yellow arrowhead) and MyoII levels at these modified contacts (C(E,N)|P(E,N+), Figure 3A,B, yellow arrowhead) were significantly reduced compared to wildtype C|P contacts (C(E,N)|P(E), Figure 3A,B, green arrowhead, Supplementary file 1 - table 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and A' and Figure 3A,B showing the Ncad localization and MyoII levels.

claim: MyoII levels at C(E,N)|P(E,N+) contacts were significantly reduced compared to wildtype C|P contacts.
source: Homophilic Ncad was detected at the C(E,N)|P(E,N+) contacts (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and A', yellow arrowhead) and MyoII levels at these modified contacts (C(E,N)|P(E,N+), Figure 3A,B, yellow arrowhead) were significantly reduced compared to wildtype C|P contacts (C(E,N)|P(E), Figure 3A,B, green arrowhead, Supplementary file 1 - table 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3A,B and Supplementary file 1 - table 1 showing the MyoII quantification.

claim: Homophilic Ncad reduces MyoII level.
source: This confirms our hypothesis that homophilic Ncad reduces MyoII level (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3C showing the MyoII quantification.

claim: Higher level of MyoII was detected at contacts between primary pigment cells with one of them misexpressing Ncad (P(E)|P(E,N+)) than at contacts between wildtype primary pigment cells expressing only Ecad (P(E)|P(E)).
source: In addition, higher level of MyoII was detected at contacts between primary pigment cells with one of them misexpressing Ncad (P(E)|P(E,N+)) (Figure 3A,D red arrowhead) than at contacts between wildtype primary pigment cells expressing only Ecad (P(E)|P(E)) (Figure 3A,B,D, Supplementary file 1 -table 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3A,D and Supplementary file 1 -table 1 showing the MyoII quantification.

claim: MyoII regulation by Ncad is not specific to the retina.
source: To test whether such property of Ncad is specific to the retinal epithelium or more general, we performed clonal misexpression of Ncad in the larval wing pouch which cells express only Ecad. We noticed higher level of MyoII at the boundary of clones compared to MyoII inside the clones or to the surrounding wildtype tissue (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C, cyan arrowheads). This indicates that MyoII regulation by Ncad is not specific to the retina.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C showing MyoII accumulation in wing disc clones.

claim: MyoII maximum intensity was systematically shifted towards the cell that expressed both Ecad and Ncad at C(E,N)|P(E) contacts.
source: We found that MyoII maximum intensity was systematically shifted towards the cell that expressed both Ecad and Ncad (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B showing the intensity profiles.

claim: The distance between MyoII and Ecad intensity peaks was found larger than the imprecision in peaks' localization.
source: Importantly, the distance between MyoII and Ecad intensity peaks (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C) was found larger than the imprecision in peaks' localization (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D, See Material and methods).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D showing the measurements.

claim: MyoII is enriched in the cortex of an Ecad- and Ncad-expressing cell when it is apposed to an Ecad-expressing cell.
source: This significant and systematic shift indicates that MyoII is enriched in the cortex of an Ecad- and Ncad-expressing cell when it is apposed to an Ecad-expressing cell (Figure 3E–G).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3E–G showing the asymmetric distribution.

claim: A symmetric localization of MyoII was observed at C(E,N)|C(E,N) contacts.
source: In contrast, we observed a symmetric localization of MyoII at C(E,N)|C(E,N) contacts (Figure 3—figure supplement 2F,H).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 2F,H showing the symmetric distribution.

claim: The increase in MyoII level is cell contact autonomous.
source: This increase in MyoII level is cell contact autonomous: we observed higher MyoII intensity at C(E,N)|P(E) contacts, irrespective of the other contacts of the cell (for instance, C(E,N)|C(E,N)).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on experimental observations.

claim: An asymmetric localization of MyoII in cells that express both Ecad and Ncad was observed at the P(E)|P(E,N+) contacts.
source: To further confirm the above observation, Ncad was again misexpressed in primary pigment cells to check if it could induce MyoII asymmetry at the modified P(E)|P(E,N+) contacts. An asymmetric localization of MyoII in cells that express both Ecad and Ncad was observed at the P(E)|P(E,N+) contacts (Figure 3H–J).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3H–J showing the asymmetric distribution.

claim: Truncated Ncad can form adhesion bonds but cannot interact with the actomyosin network.
source: To further explore how Ncad at heterotypic contacts could induce MyoII contractility, we expressed only the extracellular part of Ncad in one primary pigment cell (Figure 4A, white +). Such truncated Ncad can form adhesion bonds but cannot interact with the actomyosin network (Figure 4A, white arrowhead).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4A showing the truncated Ncad expression.

claim: A change in contact shape and MyoII levels was observed at the interface between the wildtype cone cell and primary pigment cell that misexpressed extracellular Ncad.
source: We observed a change in contact shape and MyoII levels at the interface between the wildtype cone cell and primary pigment cell that misexpressed extracellular Ncad (Figure 4B–D, compare blue and red arrowheads, Supplementary file 1 -table 1), which confirms a role for homophilic Ncad bonds in the downregulation of MyoII contractility.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B–D and Supplementary file 1 -table 1 showing the changes.

claim: Homophilic Ncad bonds play a role in the downregulation of MyoII contractility.
source: We observed a change in contact shape and MyoII levels at the interface between the wildtype cone cell and primary pigment cell that misexpressed extracellular Ncad (Figure 4B–D, compare blue and red arrowheads, Supplementary file 1 -table 1), which confirms a role for homophilic Ncad bonds in the downregulation of MyoII contractility.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B–D and Supplementary file 1 -table 1 showing the experimental results.

claim: MyoII levels at the contact between primary pigment cells, which included one cell that misexpressed extracellular Ncad showed no change in MyoII, when compared to full-length Ncad.
source: However, MyoII levels at the contact between primary pigment cells, which included one cell that misexpressed extracellular Ncad showed no change in MyoII, when compared to full-length Ncad (Figure 4B,C,E, green arrowhead, Supplementary file 1 -table 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B,C,E and Supplementary file 1 -table 1 showing the MyoII quantification.

claim: Cytoplasmic part of Ncad is required for the accumulation of MyoII at the C(E,N)|P(E) contacts.
source: This result suggested that cytoplasmic part of Ncad is required for the accumulation of MyoII at the C(E,N)|P(E) contacts.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the experimental results with truncated Ncad.

claim: While homophilic Ncad reduces MyoII contractility at homotypic contacts, unbound Ncad is able to activate MyoII, and locally enhance contractility at heterotypic contacts through its cytoplasmic part.
source: The above data suggest that while homophilic Ncad reduces MyoII contractility at homotypic contacts, unbound Ncad is able to activate MyoII, and locally enhance contractility at heterotypic contacts through its cytoplasmic part.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and summarizes the experimental findings.

claim: The perimeter after relaxation was found to be typically 8% smaller (8.4 ± 1.2, n = 7) than prior to ablation.
source: After ablation, cells relaxed towards a circular shape in the plane of adherens junctions (Video 3). Note that the perimeter after relaxation was found to be typically 8% smaller (8.4 ± 1.2, n = 7) than prior to ablation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C showing the measurements.

claim: The best fit corresponds to K = 4.2 (in units of γC(E,N)|C(E,N)=1).
source: We simulated the wildtype and four different NcadM19 mosaic ommatidia, and applied a weighted least squares method to fit them altogether (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B). The best fit corresponds to K = 4.2 (in units of γC(E,N)|C(E,N)=1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 2B showing the fitting results.

claim: The cell patterns obtained in silico for K = 4.2 are in very good agreement with the cell patterns observed in vivo, for wildtype ommatidia and for NcadM19 mosaic ommatidia with different numbers and combinations of wildtype and NcadM19 cone cells.
source: The cell patterns obtained in silico for this value are in very good agreement with the cell patterns observed in vivo, for wildtype ommatidia and for NcadM19 mosaic ommatidia with different numbers and combinations of wildtype and NcadM19 cone cells (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2C,D showing the comparison.

claim: Elastic tension contributes to 1/3 to 1/2 of the total interfacial tension, depending on the cell contacts considered.
source: Interestingly, our estimate of K also indicates that elastic tension contributes to 1/3 to 1/2 of the total interfacial tension, depending on the cell contacts considered (Figure 5—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 2E showing the tension components.

claim: MyoII has a very significant contribution to local tension, which is about two to five times higher than that of Ncad or Ecad depending on the contact type.
source: We found that MyoII has a very significant contribution to local tension, which is about two to five times higher than that of Ncad or Ecad depending on the contact type (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5D showing the relative contributions.

claim: Control of cell shape by adhesion is mostly indirect, through the regulation of MyoII level by unbound Ncad.
source: This data, in agreement with in vitro experiments on cell doublets (Maître et al., 2012), emphasizes the quantitative role of MyoII on cell shapes in vivo. It also indicates that control of cell shape by adhesion is mostly indirect, through the regulation of MyoII level by unbound Ncad.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Maître et al., 2012.

claim: Myosin-II light chain loss of function (SqhAx3) mutant leads to a massive increase in cell apical area in the mutant cells and change in cell contact length.
source: We first decreased MyoII contractility using Myosin-II light chain loss of function (SqhAx3) mutant (Figure 5E,E'), and observed a massive increase in cell apical area in the mutant cells and change in cell contact length (Figure 5—figure supplement 4A Supplementary file 1 - table 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5E,E' and Figure 5—figure supplement 4A showing the changes.

claim: Misexpression of constitutively active form of MyoII (SqhT20E.S21E) leads to a reduction of cell apical area.
source: Conversely, misexpression of constitutively active form of MyoII (SqhT20E.S21E) leads to a reduction of cell apical area (Figure 5F,F') and change in cell contact length (Figure 5—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5F,F' and Figure 5—figure supplement 4B showing the changes.

claim: Shape changes resulting from MyoII loss of function or misexpression are dominated by cell-scale (apical MyoII) rather than cell contact-scale contribution of MyoII.
source: These changes in apical area suggest that shape changes resulting from MyoII loss of function or misexpression are dominated by cell-scale (apical MyoII) rather than cell contact-scale contribution of MyoII.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the experimental observations.

claim: Wildtype cone cells undergo stereotypic neighbor exchanges.
source: Wildtype cone cells undergo stereotypic neighbor exchanges (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6A showing the time-lapse images.

claim: Anterior and posterior cells lose A-P contact, while equatorial and polar cells intercalate and form a new Eq-Pl contact (A-P to Eq-Pl contact transition).
source: Anterior and posterior cells lose A-P contact, while equatorial and polar cells intercalate and form a new Eq-Pl contact (A-P to Eq-Pl contact transition) (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5A showing the cell arrangement.

claim: 98.2% of analyzed ommatidia where Ncad was mutated in either the equatorial or polar cell failed to transit.
source: However, when imaging the NcadM19 mosaic mutants, we observed defects of this A-P to Eq-Pl transition. 98,2% of analyzed ommatidia where Ncad was mutated in either the equatorial or polar cell failed to transit (Figure 6B, red arrowheads, Figure 6C, n = 114).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6B,C showing the defects.

claim: 100% of analyzed ommatidia where Ncad was mutated in both equatorial and polar cells failed to transit.
source: 100% of analyzed ommatidia where Ncad was mutated in both equatorial and polar cells failed to transit (Figure 6D, n = 16).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6D showing the defects.

claim: The transition might be prevented due to the increase in tension at the transverse cell contacts where C(E,N)|C(E,N) contacts are transformed into C(E,N)|C(E) contacts.
source: We reasoned that this transition might be prevented due to the increase in tension at the transverse cell contacts where C(E,N)|C(E,N) contacts are transformed into C(E,N)|C(E) contacts, and indeed observed increased levels of MyoII in these contacts (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6E,F showing the increased MyoII levels.

claim: The model predicts an energy minimum in the vertical configuration in both cases (when either 1 or 2 of the polar and equatorial cells are Ncad mutants).
source: To further test this hypothesis, we estimated the energy of the system as a function of the central junction length in both vertical and horizontal configurations (Figure 6G,H). Note that this required to fix that length during the minimization process. We found that the model predicts an energy minimum in the vertical configuration in both cases (when either 1 or 2 of the polar and equatorial cells are Ncad mutants), consistent with our experimental observations.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6G,H showing the energy profiles.

claim: Cell mechanical properties, indirectly controlled by Ncad expression, not only impact on cell shapes but also on cell arrangement.
source: Thus, cell mechanical properties, indirectly controlled by Ncad expression, not only impact on cell shapes but also on cell arrangement.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and summarizes the findings.

claim: The adhesion provided by Ecad and Ncad homophilic bonds have a moderate direct contribution to interfacial tension as compared to MyoII dependent contractile forces.
source: We showed that the adhesion provided by Ecad and Ncad homophilic bonds have a moderate direct contribution to interfacial tension as compared to MyoII dependent contractile forces.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and summarizes the main finding.

claim: In vivo, the contribution of adhesion to interfacial tension is roughly half of MyoII cortical tension.
source: Our in vivo findings are consistent with in vitro measurements using the shapes of cell doublets to infer the relative contribution of adhesion and cortical tension to interfacial tension (Maître et al., 2012). Here we demonstrate that in vivo, the contribution of adhesion to interfacial tension is roughly half of MyoII cortical tension.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Maître et al., 2012.

claim: The balance of contractility and adhesion determines cell shapes, cell arrangement and cell sorting.
source: Our data indicate that the hypotheses of differential contractility (Harris, 1976; Brodland, 2002) or differential adhesion (Steinberg, 1963) are not mutually exclusive, and the balance of contractility and adhesion determines cell shapes, cell arrangement (Lecuit and Lenne, 2007; Käfer et al., 2007; Hilgenfeldt et al., 2008) and cell sorting (Krieg et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The moderate contribution of adhesion bonds to interfacial tension might explain why cadherin binding affinities are not predictive of cell sorting outcomes in vivo and in vitro.
source: The moderate contribution of adhesion bonds to interfacial tension might explain why cadherin binding affinities are not predictive of cell sorting outcomes in vivo and in vitro (Shi et al., 2008; Leckband and Sivasankar, 2012).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Shi et al., 2008; Leckband and Sivasankar, 2012.

claim: Actomyosin contractility generates a cell-scale elastic tension at the cell periphery, which restricts cell deformation.
source: Our work unravels a cell-scale (autonomous) and a junction-scale (non-autonomous) control of cell shape through actomyosin contractility. Following previous models of epithelial mechanics (Käfer et al., 2007; Hilgenfeldt et al., 2008), we confirm that actomyosin contractility generates a cell-scale elastic tension at the cell periphery, which restricts cell deformation.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Käfer et al., 2007; Hilgenfeldt et al., 2008.

claim: Cell elasticity is crucial to stabilizing the four-cone cell arrangement.
source: Our model shows that the cell-scale elasticity is crucial to stabilizing the four-cone cell arrangement and it is possible that cell elasticity also ensures correct global patterning of the retina.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the modeling results.

claim: MyoII contractility contributes locally to tension at cell contacts (cortical tension) to shape cone cell arrangement.
source: Analysis of our measurements of mechanical properties and quantification of molecular distribution demonstrate that MyoII contractility also contributes locally to tension at cell contacts (cortical tension) to shape cone cell arrangement.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the experimental and modeling results.

claim: The local contribution of MyoII to tension was not considered in previous works.
source: This local contribution of MyoII to tension was not considered in previous works (Käfer et al., 2007; Hilgenfeldt et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Käfer et al., 2007; Hilgenfeldt et al., 2008.

claim: The cell-scale elasticity and junction-scale cortical tension contributions are on the same order of magnitude and are both crucial to predicting cell shape.
source: The cell-scale elasticity and junction-scale cortical tension contributions are on the same order of magnitude (Figure 5—figure supplement 2E) and are both crucial to predicting cell shape.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 2E showing the tension components.

claim: Junctional N-cadherin bonds yield contact expansion between Ncad-expressing cells.
source: We identified a dual role of Ncad on cell shapes and cell arrangement. Junctional N-cadherin bonds yield contact expansion between Ncad-expressing cells.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and summarizes the findings.

claim: The effect of junctional N-cadherin bonds on contact expansion is moderate and cannot alone account for the shapes of cells in the ommatidia.
source: However, this effect is moderate and cannot alone account for the shapes of cells in the ommatidia.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the experimental results.

claim: Heterotypic contacts between cells expressing Ecad and Ncad and cells expressing Ecad only exhibit increased local contractility as compared to homotypic contacts.
source: Through the determination of MyoII distributions at cell contacts, we uncovered another mechanism mediated by Ncad at heterotypic cell contacts, where a low level of Ncad is detected at junctional plane (unbound). Heterotypic contacts between cells expressing Ecad and Ncad and cells expressing Ecad only exhibit increased local contractility as compared to homotypic contacts.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is based on the experimental observations.

claim: The difference in contractility at heterotypic contacts cannot be explained only by differences in adhesion contributed by both Ecad and Ncad.
source: This difference in contractility cannot be explained only by differences in adhesion contributed by both Ecad and Ncad.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the analysis of the data.

claim: Increased contractility at heterotypic contacts is a junction-autonomous property.
source: This is a junction-autonomous property, as in an Ecad- and Ncad-expressing cell (C), we observed increased contractility at heterotypic contacts irrespective of the other contacts of the cell (heterotypic and/or homotypic).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the experimental observations.

claim: Unbound Ncad has the ability to redirect MyoII at heterotypic contacts via its signaling intracellular region.
source: Our data suggest that unbound Ncad has the ability to redirect MyoII at heterotypic contacts via its signaling intracellular region.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is based on the experimental results with truncated Ncad.

claim: N-cadherin was found to polarize MyoII contractility directly through its cytoplasmic partners such as β-catenin or indirectly through its interplay with Ecad.
source: Interestingly, this does not seem to be specific to the retina and might be a more general mechanism, as suggested by our observations in the larval wing disc. N-cadherin was found to polarize MyoII contractility directly through it cytoplasmic partners such as β-catenin (Ouyang et al., 2013) or indirectly through its interplay with Ecad (Scarpa et al., 2015), presumably through an indirect mechanism.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Ouyang et al., 2013 and Scarpa et al., 2015.

claim: Cadherin-mediated adhesion is tightly coupled to actomyosin through small GTPase including Rho and antagonistic Rac.
source: Cadherin-mediated adhesion is tightly coupled to actomyosin through small GTPase including Rho and antagonistic Rac (Takeichi et al., 1997; Ratheesh et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Takeichi et al., 1997; Ratheesh et al., 2013.

claim: Homophilic N-cadherin dimerization activates Rho and Rac.
source: Homophilic N-cadherin dimerization activates Rho (Comunale et al., 2007; Charrasse et al., 2002; Marrs et al., 2009; Taulet et al., 2009; Puvirajesinghe et al., 2016) and Rac (Matsuda et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by multiple citations.

claim: High MyoII contractility induced by cell contact molecules at tissue boundary has a significant impact on tissue separation.
source: High MyoII contractility induced by cell contact molecules at tissue boundary has a significant impact on tissue separation (Dahmann et al., 2011; Major and Irvine, 2006; Fagotto, 2014).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Dahmann et al., 2011; Major and Irvine, 2006; Fagotto, 2014.

claim: Supracellular actomyosin structures are found at boundaries in wing imaginal discs and embryos.
source: In Drosophila, supracellular actomyosin structures are found at boundaries in wing imaginal discs (Major and Irvine, 2006; Landsberg et al., 2009; Monier et al., 2010; Umetsu et al., 2014; Bielmeier et al., 2016) and embryos (Monier et al., 2010; Röper, 2013; Laplante and Nilson, 2011).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The four cone cells in ommatidia form a boundary with primary pigment cells through increased MyoII contractility at the C(E,N)|P(E) heterotypic contacts.
source: We show here that the four cone cells in ommatidia form a boundary with primary pigment cells through increased MyoII contractility at the C(E,N)|P(E) heterotypic contacts.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the experimental findings.

claim: The MyoII cable at the boundary of cone cells and primary pigment cells is reminiscent of that triggered by Crumbs anisotropy at the border of placodes in the Drosophila.
source: This MyoII cable is reminiscent of that triggered by Crumbs anisotropy at the border of placodes in the Drosophila (Röper, 2012).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Röper, 2012.

claim: In the retina, accumulation of MyoII is junction-autonomous and determined by the expression of adhesive molecules in the apposed cells.
source: In the retina, we showed that accumulation of MyoII is junction-autonomous and determined by the expression of adhesive molecules in the apposed cells.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and summarizes the findings.

claim: MyoII is asymmetrically distributed at heterotypic contacts, mainly localized at the cortex of the Ecad and Ncad expressing cells.
source: At the heterotypic contacts, MyoII is asymmetrically distributed: it is mainly localized at the cortex of the Ecad and Ncad expressing cells.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the experimental observations.

claim: The asymmetry of MyoII suggests that tension can be set and modified asymmetrically.
source: From a mechanical point of view, the asymmetry of MyoII is an interesting observation as it suggests that tension can be set and modified asymmetrically.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is based on the interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Shrinkage or extension of a junction might be driven unilaterally from one of the two apposed cells.
source: As a consequence, shrinkage or extension of a junction might be driven unilaterally from one of the two apposed cells.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is based on the interpretation of the asymmetric MyoII distribution.

claim: Asymmetrically distributed unbound Ncad could signal to MyoII and cause its asymmetry.
source: The adhesion molecules that are engaged in trans-bonds at cell contacts are symmetric in the apposed membranes. Thus, they cannot be the direct cause of this asymmetry. Instead, our data suggest that asymmetrically distributed unbound Ncad could signal to MyoII and cause its asymmetry.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is based on the experimental results.

claim: High MyoII contractility at contacts between two cell types might represent a general mechanism, which could be important for lineage sorting and elimination of misspecified cells.
source: High MyoII contractility at contacts between two cell types might represent a general mechanism, which could be important for lineage sorting and elimination of misspecified cells (Bielmeier et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Bielmeier et al., 2016.

claim: Given the importance of E- to N-cadherin switch in epithelial-mesenchyme transition, the findings may have implications in other developmental processes.
source: Given the importance of E- to N-cadherin switch in epithelial-mesenchyme transition (Wheelock et al., 2008), our findings may also have implications in other developmental processes.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Wheelock et al., 2008.
